official_title.value: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo- Controlled, Phase 3 Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Baricitinib in Adult Patients With Severe or Very Severe Alopecia Areata

mechanism_of_action.source_excerpt: openFDA drug/label mechanism_of_action (FDA-approved label, section 12.1) -- extracted text: 12.1 Mechanism of Action Baricitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor. JAKs are intracellular enzymes which transmit signals arising from cytokine or growth factor-receptor interactions on the cellular membrane to influence cellular processes of hematopoiesis and immune cell function. Within the signaling pathway, JAKs phosphorylate and activate Signal Transducers and Activators of Transcription (STATs) which modulate intracellular activity including gene expression. Baricitinib modulates the signaling pathway at the point of JAKs, preventing the phosphorylation and activation of STATs. JAK enzymes transmit cytokine signaling through their pairing (e.g., JAK1/JAK2, JAK1/JAK3, JAK1/TYK2, JAK2/JAK2, JAK2/TYK2). In cell-free isolated enzyme assays, baricitinib had greater inhibitory potency at JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 relative to JAK3. In human leukocytes, baricitinib inhibited cytokine induced STAT phosphorylation mediated by JAK1/JAK2, JAK1/JAK3, JAK1/TYK2, or JAK2/TYK2 with comparable potencies. However, the relevance of inhibition of specific JAK enzymes to therapeutic effectiveness is not currently known.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: Protocol Section 10.3.1.3: 'Multiplicity adjusted analyses will be performed on the primary and key secondary objectives in order to control the overall family-wise Type I error rate at a 2-sided alpha level of 0.05. The graphical multiple testing procedure described in Bretz et al. (2011) will be used. The graphical approach is a closed testing procedure; hence, it strongly controls the familywise error rate across all endpoints (Alosh et al. 2014).' SAP Section 6.1: '...based on a 2-sided Fisher's exact test within the graphical testing scheme, at an initial significance level of 0.04 for 4-mg dose and 0.01 for 2-mg dose.' SAP Section 6.6, Step 1: 'The primary endpoint SALT <=20 will be first tested at a 2-sided alpha=0.025 for both 2-mg and 4-mg doses. If neither of the null hypotheses is rejected, no further testing is conducted... If at least 1 of null hypotheses is rejected, the testing process continues to Step 2, with the remaining alpha propagated according to the weights on the corresponding edges.'

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Study Design: 'The study design includes 5 periods: a 5-week screening period; a 36-week double-blind, placebo-controlled treatment period; a 68-week long-term extension period; a 96-week bridging extension; and a posttreatment follow-up period. Period 1: Screening period (Visit 1) is between 3 and 35 days prior to Visit 2 (Week 0). Period 2: 36-week double-blind, placebo-controlled treatment period is from Week 0 (Baseline; Visit 2) to Week 36 (Visit 8). Period 3: 68-week, long-term extension period with randomized withdrawal (for responders) is from Week 36 (Visit 8) to Week 104 (Visit 18). Period 4: Bridging Extension: from Week 104 (Visit 18) and up to Week 200 (Visit 24)... Period 5: Posttreatment follow-up period; the posttreatment follow-up visit should occur approximately 4 weeks after the last dose of investigational product.' Patients randomized 2:2:3 to placebo, baricitinib 2-mg, or baricitinib 4-mg QD 'for up to 200 weeks.'

value.applies_to_period: Week 36 onward (double-blind placebo-controlled period ends at Week 36; subsequent rescue/downtitration occurs in the long-term extension period, Weeks 36-104)
value.rationale: This is a dose-adjustment/rescue design specific to a long-duration JAK-inhibitor AA trial, not a topical/systemic escalation ladder. Core rule (Section 'At Week 36'): 'Patients in the placebo treatment arm who have not achieved a SALT <=20 at Week 36 will be rescued to baricitinib and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to baricitinib 2-mg dose or baricitinib 4-mg dose.' Patients on placebo who achieved SALT<=20 by Week 36 remain on placebo until Week 52; if they experience a >20-point absolute worsening in SALT after Week 52 they are rescued to baricitinib 2-mg. Baricitinib-arm patients (2-mg since baseline) who remain non-responders (SALT>20) at Week 52 are rescued to 4-mg. This rescue/downtitration state machine continues in further detail through Weeks 52 and 76 (see protocol Summary of Study Design), well beyond the primary Week-36 double-blind endpoint window that this schema field is centered on.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Summary of Study Design, 'At Week 36': 'Patients in the placebo treatment arm who have not achieved a SALT <=20 at Week 36 will be rescued to baricitinib and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to baricitinib 2-mg dose or baricitinib 4-mg dose. Patients in the placebo arm who have achieved a SALT <=20 at Week 36 will remain on placebo... until Week 52, even if a relapse is observed between Week 36 and Week 52.' 'At Week 52... Responders who experience a loss of treatment benefit after Week 52 (defined as >20-point absolute worsening in total SALT score)... had remained on placebo since Baseline (Visit 2), will be rescued to baricitinib 2-mg.'
